title: Realtime Runtime Protocol 1.0 Core Conformance Scenarios
description: Transport-independent black-box scenarios. Each scenario must assert behavior and the diagnostic boundary evidence named in diagnostics.

given: transport is open
contract digest matches
scenarios.when: client sends session.open as its first application message within the deadline
then: server returns exactly one session.ready
session generation is positive
capabilities and heartbeat policy are explicit

given: transport is open
scenarios.when: client sends no session.open before the 10 second deadline
then: server emits RT_SESSION_INIT_TIMEOUT when possible
transport closes
no session resources remain

given: session.open was already received
scenarios.when: client sends a second session.open on the same transport
then: server rejects the protocol violation
transport closes
the existing principal is not replaced

given: client and server contract digests differ
scenarios.when: client opens a session
then: server returns RT_CONTRACT_INCOMPATIBLE
no stream or command operation is accepted

given: a ready session
credential is approaching expiry
scenarios.when: server sends session.auth.challenge and the provider returns fresh credentials
then: one credential request is in flight
client sends session.auth.update
server increments auth generation
active streams are reauthorized before paused delivery resumes
physical transport is not reconnected

given: a ready session
credentials are expired or revoked
scenarios.when: refresh fails or its deadline expires
then: new commands and subscriptions fail or remain paused according to error disposition
application delivery does not continue under stale authorization
heartbeat may continue until session rejection

given: negotiated application heartbeat
scenarios.when: server sends heartbeat.ping
then: client promptly returns heartbeat.pong with the same pingId
no domain state changes

given: an apparently open but half-closed connection
scenarios.when: matching pong is absent for the negotiated timeout
then: server closes the transport
client enters reconnect backoff
session and streams become suspended

given: browser execution was suspended in the background beyond the heartbeat window
scenarios.when: document becomes visible and the connection is stale
then: client immediately replaces the stale transport
normal replay or resync semantics apply
no false continuity is claimed

given: multiple concurrent stream consumers
one transport failure
scenarios.when: recovery starts
then: exactly one physical reconnect loop runs
each logical stream resubscribes after session.ready
retries are jittered and bounded by policy

given: resume token is missing, invalid, or expired
fresh authentication succeeds
scenarios.when: client reconnects
then: session.ready reports resumeStatus unavailable or fresh
client explicitly resubscribes from each last applied cursor
runtime does not infer server-restored rooms

given: resume token belongs to another principal, tenant, audience, or contract
scenarios.when: client attempts resume
then: resume continuity is denied
token does not authenticate the client
no cross-boundary state is restored

given: client last applied cursor is retained
missed events remain in durable retention
scenarios.when: client resubscribes after disconnect
then: server declares replay head
events after cursor are delivered in stream order
live events are buffered until replay.complete
client converges to the declared head

given: the same eventId arrives with two deliveryIds
scenarios.when: client processes both attempts
then: domain reducer applies exactly once
both delivery attempts remain observable
cursor never regresses

given: per-stream ordering and gap detection are negotiated
scenarios.when: sequence N+2 arrives after N without N+1
then: N+2 is not silently applied as contiguous
client requests replay or fenced resync
gap scope identifies the stream

given: requested cursor is outside replay retention
scenarios.when: server selects snapshot recovery
then: snapshot state and cursor are atomically consistent
events after snapshot cursor through the declared head are retained and applied
live delivery is released only after the fence

given: live events exceed the recovery buffer count or byte bound during replay or snapshot
scenarios.when: overflow occurs
then: server or client emits RT_RECOVERY_OVERFLOW
partial recovery is not presented as complete
a fresh fenced snapshot starts or the stream fails explicitly

given: server durably accepts a command
receipt is lost before reaching the client
scenarios.when: client reconnects within idempotency and result retention
then: client queries status or retries using the same commandId
new commandAttemptId identifies the wire attempt
domain effect occurs once
outcome converges

given: command outcome is beyond idempotency or result retention
scenarios.when: client asks for status
then: server reports expired or unknown
runtime does not retry as though exactly-once were guaranteed
user-visible policy can request reconciliation

given: a user clicks the same action twice
scenarios.when: application calls execute twice without an explicit idempotencyKey
then: two distinct commandIds are created
the runtime does not collapse intentional operations
each attempt is independently observable

given: command is completed by the server
causal event is not yet applied by the client
scenarios.when: application awaits settlement
then: completed may resolve
observed remains pending
observed resolves only after the causal event is applied

given: transport is open
scenarios.when: peer sends malformed JSON or a schema-invalid message
then: message is not dispatched
structured RT_MESSAGE_INVALID is emitted when safe
repeated or fatal violations close the transport

given: reference server maxMessageBytes is 1048576
scenarios.when: peer sends a larger message
then: server rejects it before unbounded allocation
transport or message scope error is explicit
no application handler runs

given: a client or stream cannot consume at producer rate
scenarios.when: configured pending byte or record bound is reached
then: declared coalesce, resync, or disconnect policy runs
memory remains bounded
loss or resync is explicit

given: React Strict Mode, HMR, and repeated mount/unmount or subscribe/unsubscribe churn
scenarios.when: the cycle repeats after warm-up
then: only one physical runtime remains per configured scope
listener, timer, subscription, buffer, and pending-command counts return to baseline
heap and active handles plateau

given: an adapter cannot prove durable replay or fenced snapshots
scenarios.when: session negotiates capabilities
then: unsupported fields are false or none
client never silently runs the stronger recovery path
operations requiring the missing guarantee fail or downgrade explicitly

given: an event and outbox row committed
one or more outbox workers
scenarios.when: a worker claims the row and crashes at any point around notify and commit
then: pg_notify and notify_committed_at become visible together or neither becomes visible
another worker can reclaim rolled-back work
event-table catch-up converges without relying on notification delivery

given: Gateway A and Gateway B authenticate the same canonical identity for the first time
scenarios.when: both create or rotate identity aliases concurrently
then: exactly one durable principalNamespaceId is selected
every alias version points to that namespace
raw issuer and subject are absent from command and diagnostic records

given: commandResultRetentionMs and idempotencyRetentionMs are negotiated
the same command ID is retried
scenarios.when: the retry occurs before result expiry, during tombstone-only retention, or after idempotency expiry
then: the capability invariant is positive result retention not exceeding idempotency retention
same canonical intent never creates another effect within idempotency retention
different intent is explicitly rejected
after idempotency retention status is unknown and the client does not resend

given: two principals share a tenant and issuer
scenarios.when: one principal queries the other's command ID or attempts its stream cursor
then: wire output does not reveal whether the foreign resource exists
the operation returns unknown or an indistinguishable generic rejection
specific authorization denial remains internal diagnostic evidence

given: a command effect committed
its acknowledgement was lost
the event is at or before a later authoritative snapshot cursor
scenarios.when: status reconciliation returns the producer-issued causal event position after the snapshot is applied
then: completed resolves from durable status
the snapshot sequence proves causal inclusion for the exact event ID and stream
observed settles without duplicate event application
the pending command is released

given: a PostgreSQL gateway already has ready sessions
scenarios.when: database, listener, or outbox health becomes unavailable
then: readiness becomes false
existing sessions do not receive new durable receipts or successful durable replay or snapshot claims
operations receive structured retry or failure and sessions drain within a bound when safety cannot be restored

given: a replay selection fault is injected
scenarios.when: client fails to converge
then: evidence distinguishes server replay selection from transport delivery and client reducer application
first divergent boundary is identified
capture gaps prevent unsupported certainty

given: a browser operation crosses Gateway A, PostgreSQL, and Gateway B
scenarios.when: doctor evaluates recovery
then: the topology manifest names each required runtimeId and runtimeBootId
cross-runtime order follows explicit causal handoffs rather than producer-local recordSequence
a missing required instance prevents proven completeness
SIGKILL evidence loss is partial and indeterminate

given: PostgreSQL committed a transaction
the node-postgres caller did not receive the COMMIT acknowledgement
scenarios.when: the operation reconciles on a fresh connection
then: the original attempt is indeterminate rather than rolled back
same-connection ROLLBACK is cleanup evidence only
the operation serializes under its stable identity before inspecting durable state
only exact transaction-scoped durable proof resolves committed or rolled back
an unresolved attempt prevents a proven doctor verdict

given: an append has a caller-provided stable operation identity
its COMMIT acknowledgement is lost
scenarios.when: the caller retries the same append identity
then: the same versioned canonical append intent, including effect schema and effect-defining payload, returns the one durable event
domain mutation and outbox append occur exactly once
different event or effect intent under the same identity is rejected
automatic retry never creates a second effect

given: a REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY snapshot transaction
its COMMIT acknowledgement is unavailable
scenarios.when: the provider discards the attempt and obtains a successful fresh snapshot
then: the failed acknowledgement is not called rollback
no snapshot success is emitted for the discarded attempt
the original transaction resolves only as no durable effect after the retry succeeds
all failed retries leave the operation indeterminate

given: an original transaction aborts after COMMIT invocation becomes unobservable
a queued competitor commits the same command, append, principal alias, or outbox operation
scenarios.when: the original caller reconciles
then: the competitor proves operation convergence only
the original transaction is resolved from its exact durable attempt marker
no competitor event or marker is attributed to the original transaction ID

given: schema migration, command retention, outbox retention, or stream retention writes
the COMMIT acknowledgement is lost
scenarios.when: the write reconciles
then: the path uses the centralized transaction outcome model rather than implicit autocommit
the exact attempt marker proves the result
a bounded unresolved path remains indeterminate

given: a transaction requires cleanup or reconciliation
ROLLBACK fails or the connection pool is exhausted
scenarios.when: the deadline expires
then: the uncertain connection is destroyed rather than returned to the pool
cleanup is not outcome proof
cleanup and connection acquisition are included in the reconciliation deadline
no durable success is claimed

given: one outbox transaction claims multiple events
its COMMIT outcome is indeterminate
scenarios.when: doctor evaluates any claimed event journey
then: that event carries the exact batch transaction link
another batch or older publish cannot satisfy the boundary
unresolved evidence prevents proven

given: one portable Draft 2020-12 contract defines streams events and commands
scenarios.when: client React and server APIs consume the contract
then: member names and payloads are inferred without consumer generics
unknown members and incompatible payloads fail compilation
every external runtime payload is schema validated
contract digest mismatch fails explicitly

given: a built package tarball
a consumer project outside the monorepo workspace
scenarios.when: the consumer installs typechecks builds and runs the React and Node entries
then: no workspace symlink source import private path or tsconfig mapping is required
browser entries do not load Node server modules
Node server entry composes the durable PostgreSQL profile
the installed package identity and release metadata match the approved public contract

given: tenant-scoped payload-redacted evidence
a local or explicitly injected read-only source
scenarios.when: CLI and MCP query doctor command stream resource or raw evidence
then: both surfaces use the same analyzer result
every page reports bounds cursor omission ranges and completeness
tenant mismatch invalid cursor and unsupported conclusions fail explicitly
incomplete evidence never becomes proven
no mutation or admin operation is exposed

given: a tenant-scoped redacted evidence snapshot
an expected producer-instance topology
scenarios.when: CLI or read-only MCP evaluates or paginates the incident
then: only manifest producer instances can satisfy required boundaries
ambiguous role-only boundaries remain indeterminate
continuation cursors are bound to the immutable source digest
top-level application identifiers are stable pseudonyms
an inventory capture proves leaks only when capture ID count and digest match

given: a reusable typed stream handle
an application contract whose physical stream keys may collide
scenarios.when: the last subscriber is released and later remounts or a client requests an ambiguous stream
then: the released terminal entry is replaced by a fresh idle entry
the ambiguous request invokes no application handler
the request fails generically without changing database readiness
application error text cannot impersonate an infrastructure outage

given: two streams use the same event member name
durable payload shapes have independent explicit schema identities
scenarios.when: a payload shape changes from version one to version two
then: the streams may declare different schema identities
the changed shape uses a new positive integer schema version
the manifest digest changes
a version-one durable event is not validated as version two merely because its member name matches

given: a command receipt was accepted
the completion payload violates its declared result schema
scenarios.when: the client receives command.completed or completed status
then: validation runs before completed state
the local attempt rejects with a contract error
completed and observed success evidence are absent
handling only one settlement promise does not create an unhandled rejection from the other

given: doctor evaluates a cross-runtime command journey
database and server boundaries share an explicit causal handoff
scenarios.when: doctor returns a proven result and a weaker model expands its evidence reference
then: the report names the ordered matched record IDs producer instances components transaction and proof source
the conclusion-level last successful boundary cites evidence even when there is no issue
a mismatched handoff remains indeterminate
the source-bound reference expands only its bounded closure
a hidden source mutation or cursor/reference tamper is rejected

given: a client owns an open physical transport and logical command or React subscriptions
scenarios.when: transport close or listener release throws during terminal disposal
then: logical cleanup and terminal state transitions still complete
all release failures are aggregated after cleanup
a failed physical close remains a failed owned resource
leak diagnosis cannot report proven absence

given: a browser WebSocket upgrade
an exact configured Origin allowlist
scenarios.when: Origin is missing null malformed or not an exact member
then: upgrade returns forbidden before authentication
no client slot recorder or per-connection resource is allocated
Origin-less Node clients require explicit allowMissingOrigin

given: an empty dedicated PostgreSQL schema
one exact contract identity
scenarios.when: the deploy migration installs framework storage and a runtime starts
then: binding metadata records storage version namespace contract ID manifest version and manifest digest
runtime startup performs no DDL
any different contract identity member is rejected
framework SQL advisory locks operation correlations and the notification channel remain namespace-scoped

given: resume auth refresh and foreground replacement are protocol-defined
the alpha runtime does not implement them
scenarios.when: a peer attempts an unsupported alpha behavior
then: the server issues no unusable resume credential
auth refresh fails the session explicitly
support metadata remains unsupported rather than verified
cursor replay and command status remain the recovery path

given: a TCP or browser WebSocket handshake never completes
scenarios.when: the configured connection deadline expires
then: the connection attempt rejects with a typed timeout
the pending physical socket is closed
the single reconnect owner can enter bounded backoff

given: many clients lose the same gateway simultaneously
scenarios.when: each schedules its next bounded reconnect attempt
then: the configured delay is an upper bound
half-to-full jitter prevents a deterministic fleet-wide retry instant
one client still owns only one reconnect timer

given: an allowed Origin
the gateway connection capacity is full
scenarios.when: another WebSocket upgrade arrives
then: the gateway returns HTTP 503 before WebSocket upgrade
no per-client resource or authentication callback is created
a retryable capacity boundary is recorded

given: authentication work times out or its bounded hook capacity is full
scenarios.when: session initialization cannot complete
then: the response is non-enumerating and retryable
the failure is not represented as invalid credentials
the transport closes with a retry-oriented status

given: a client receives retryable session.rejected or its auth provider is pending when transport closes
scenarios.when: the current initialization attempt ends
then: the client cancels current initialization
the runtime is not terminally disposed
bounded recovery state is retained
one reconnect loop continues

given: WebSocket upgrade succeeds but session.ready or session.rejected never arrives
scenarios.when: the finite session-open deadline elapses repeatedly
then: the physical transport is released
the client reconnects
exponential jitter progression is retained until session.ready
